mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the federal funds rate over three consecutive months signals a tightening monetary regime, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate cash flows, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are not significantly negative (< -1%) in at least 70% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) exceeding 2% coincident with a rise in housing starts (HOUST) predicts a rebound in consumer confidence and capital spending, driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 falls >2% YoY and HOUST rises >1% MoM
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are not significantly positive (>0%) in at least 60% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase in the unemployment rate above 6% for two consecutive months signals deteriorating labor market conditions, reducing corporate earnings expectations and leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are not significantly negative (< -1%) in at least 60% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in the industrial production index (INDPRO) below -1% for three consecutive months indicates contraction in manufacturing output, which reduces corporate revenue growth and results in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are not significantly negative (< -1%) in at least 60% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in payroll employment (PAYEMS) and a fall in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) by more than 0.3 percentage points in the same month signals a tightening labor market, which increases wage pressures and inflation expectations, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS rises and UNRATE falls >0.3pp in the same month
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day returns are not significantly positive (>0%) in at least 60% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent monthly decline in real retail sales (RSAFS) below -2% for four consecutive months indicates weakening consumer demand, which reduces revenue for consumer-facing firms and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are not significantly negative (< -1%) in at least 60% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A low and stable federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS < 1% for six consecutive months) combined with rising consumer price inflation (CPIAUCSL YoY > 2%) signals accommodative monetary policy in an inflationary environment, which historically supports equity valuations via lower real rates, producing positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS < 1% for 6 months and CPIAUCSL YoY > 2%
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are not significantly positive (>0%) in at least 60% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A consistent monthly increase in housing starts (HOUST) above 5% for three consecutive months signals a housing market recovery, which boosts construction-related equities and consumer spending, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are not significantly positive (>0%) in at least 60% of triggered episodes.
